name: 28-91 dominoes
description: 28-91 dominoes refers to block or draw domino games played with sets of 28 tiles (double-6) up to 91 tiles (double-12). Same core rules: match numbers on open ends, doubles crosswise, first out or lowest pips if blocked. Set size and player count vary.

overview.description: 28-91 dominoes refers to block or draw domino games played with sets of 28 tiles (double-6) up to 91 tiles (double-12). Same core rules: match numbers on open ends, doubles crosswise, first out or lowest pips if blocked. Set size and player count vary.

history.origins: Block/draw dominoes with set sizes from 28 (double-6) to 91 (double-12). Same core rules; larger sets allow more players or longer games.
timeline: 12th–13th century: Chinese domino tiles used in gambling games and playing-card style games.
Mid-18th century: modern Western block and draw domino games using double-six and extended sets documented in France and spreading across Europe and North America.
history.cultural: Domino games worldwide; set size varies by region.

setup.deck: Double-6 (28), double-9 (55), or double-12 (91) domino set
setup.dealing: Draw tiles (number per player depends on set size); remainder boneyard in draw variant.

rules.objective: Play all tiles first, or have fewest pips if blocked.
rules.gameplay: Highest double leads. Match one number to an open end; doubles crosswise. Block: pass if cannot play. Draw: draw from boneyard until playable. Winner scores opponents' pips or lowest hand wins if blocked.
keyRules: Match to open ends; doubles crosswise

strategy.basic: Get rid of high doubles and high tiles early; block when ahead.
strategy.intermediate: Block ends opponents need; in draw variant draw early to keep options.
strategy.advanced: Force block when you have few pips; leave awkward ends for opponents.
tips: Larger sets (55, 91) allow more players or longer games.
Block vs draw: agree before play.

variations.name: Double-9 Set
variations.description: Played with a double-9 domino set (55 tiles) for 4-6 players.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes the physical set size and player count; the core rules and engine parameters remain the same.

scoring.description: Block: play all tiles or score lowest pips. Draw: same with boneyard.
scoring.winCondition: First to play all tiles wins, or lowest hand if blocked.
